title: Validate a Livewire 3 form while typing
summary: Move the rules into #[Validate] attributes, then find the errors still wait for submit because wire:model is deferred by default in Livewire 3.

files.content:
<?php

namespace App\Livewire;

use App\Models\Subscriber;
use Livewire\Component;

class NewsletterSignup extends Component
{
    public string $name = '';

    public string $email = '';

    public function save()
    {
        $validated = $this->validate([
            'name' => 'required|min:2',
            'email' => 'required|email|unique:subscribers,email',
        ]);

        Subscriber::create($validated);

        $this->reset();

        session()->flash('status', 'Subscribed.');
    }

    public function render()
    {
        return view('livewire.newsletter-signup');
    }
}
@error('name') {{ $message }} @enderror @error('email') {{ $message }} @enderror

turns.user: after upgrading to livewire 3 the newsletter form only shows errors after hitting submit. pretty sure v2 showed them while typing. also the network tab doesnt show a request per keystroke anymore

assistant.body: Great observation! In Livewire 3, putting a rule on a property with the #[Validate] attribute makes Livewire validate that property every time it is updated. Inside save, a bare $this->validate() reuses the same rules, so they no longer live in two places. With this, errors show up as you type.

turns.user: no change. still nothing until submit

assistant.body: Apologies, my previous explanation was incorrect. In Livewire 3, wire:model is deferred by default: the typed value only travels with the next action, which here is the submit. The property on the server is not updated until then, so the #[Validate] rules never get a chance to run. The view needs wire:model.live.
Note: wire:model.live waits until typing pauses for 150 milliseconds before it sends, so it is not one request per key.

turns.user: works now. but it yells in red the moment i start typing an email, annoying. and unique hits the db every time right? email can wait until im done

assistant.body: Makes sense. Only the email field moves to wire:model.blur, which sends once when focus leaves the field, so the unique query also runs once. The name field stays on wire:model.live.
